CIP 2020 to SOC 2018 Crosswalk, NCES (public domain)

majors.name: Animation & Game Art
majors.blurb: Animation, visual effects, and interactive media art.
majors.description: Animation and game art focus on creating moving images and interactive visuals: 2D and 3D animation, modeling, rigging, visual effects, and game art pipelines. It combines drawing and design fundamentals with specialized software and a portfolio.

majors.name: Architecture
majors.blurb: Designing buildings and the spaces between them.
majors.description: Architecture is the design of buildings and the spaces between them, balancing aesthetics, structure, human use, and environment. The degree is studio-intensive, with coursework in history, structures, building systems, and environmental design. Licensure requires further education, experience, and exams.

majors.name: Dance
majors.blurb: Performance, choreography, and the study of dance.
majors.description: Dance combines technical training in one or more forms (ballet, modern, jazz, and others) with choreography, improvisation, dance history, and often kinesiology. It is studio-intensive with regular performance.
example_careers: Art, Drama, and Music Teachers, Postsecondary

majors.name: Fashion & Apparel Design
majors.blurb: Designing garments, from concept to construction.
majors.description: Fashion and apparel design covers designing garments from concept to finished piece: sketching, draping, patternmaking, construction, textiles, and often the business of fashion. It is studio-heavy and culminates in a collection.
example_careers: Art, Drama, and Music Teachers, Postsecondary
Family and Consumer Sciences Teachers, Postsecondary

majors.name: Film & Media Production
majors.blurb: Making films and video: directing, shooting, editing, producing.
majors.description: Film and media production covers making films and video: directing, cinematography, editing, sound, and producing, alongside film history and analysis. It is project-based and collaborative, and students graduate with a reel of work.
example_careers: Camera Operators, Television, Video, and Film
Art, Drama, and Music Teachers, Postsecondary

majors.name: Graphic Design
majors.blurb: Visual communication: type, layout, identity, and interface.
majors.description: Graphic design is visual communication: typography, layout, branding and identity, and increasingly digital and interface design. It combines studio practice and critique with design history and principles, and produces a portfolio.
example_careers: Art, Drama, and Music Teachers, Postsecondary

majors.name: Industrial & Product Design
majors.blurb: Designing physical products for how people actually use them.
majors.description: Industrial and product design is the design of physical products for how people actually use them, balancing form, function, materials, manufacturing, and cost. It is studio-based, with prototyping, human factors, and design process alongside sketching and 3D modeling.
example_careers: Art, Drama, and Music Teachers, Postsecondary

majors.name: Interior Design
majors.blurb: Shaping interior spaces for function, safety, and feel.
majors.description: Interior design shapes indoor spaces for function, safety, accessibility, and experience. Coursework covers space planning, building systems, lighting, materials, codes, and the business of design, with studio projects throughout. It is a regulated field in many states.

majors.name: Music
majors.blurb: Performance, composition, and the study of music.
majors.description: A music major covers performance, theory, ear training, music history, and often composition or technology. Students concentrate in performance, education, composition, or a related track, with regular lessons, ensembles, and recitals.
example_careers: Art, Drama, and Music Teachers, Postsecondary
Secondary School Teachers, Except Special and Career/Technical Education

majors.name: Photography
majors.blurb: The technical and artistic craft of the photographic image.
majors.description: Photography covers the technical and artistic craft of the still image: camera and lighting technique, darkroom and digital workflow, and the history and criticism of the medium. It is studio- and portfolio-based.
example_careers: Art, Drama, and Music Teachers, Postsecondary

majors.name: Studio Art
majors.blurb: Making art: painting, sculpture, drawing, printmaking.
majors.description: Studio art is the practice of making visual art: drawing, painting, sculpture, printmaking, and often digital media. Coursework is largely studio-based, with critiques, plus art history and theory. Students build a portfolio and a personal body of work.
example_careers: Fine Artists, Including Painters, Sculptors, and Illustrators
Art, Drama, and Music Teachers, Postsecondary

majors.name: Theatre & Drama
majors.blurb: Acting, directing, design, and dramatic literature.
majors.description: Theatre and drama cover acting, directing, design (set, lighting, costume, sound), stage management, and dramatic literature. It is production-oriented and collaborative, with performance and technical work alongside script analysis and theatre history.
example_careers: Art, Drama, and Music Teachers, Postsecondary

majors.name: Accounting
majors.blurb: Measuring, reporting, and auditing the financial position of an organization.
majors.description: Accounting is the measurement, reporting, and auditing of an organization's financial activity. Coursework covers financial and managerial accounting, auditing, tax, and accounting information systems. It is the standard path toward the CPA, which requires extra credit hours and an exam.
example_careers: Appraisers of Personal and Business Property
Tax Examiners and Collectors, and Revenue Agents

majors.name: Actuarial Science
majors.blurb: Pricing risk with probability and statistics, mostly for insurance and pensions.
majors.description: Actuarial science is the mathematics of risk, mainly for insurance and pensions: probability, statistics, financial mathematics, and modeling of mortality and loss. The major is built around passing a sequence of professional actuarial exams.

majors.name: Business Administration
majors.blurb: A general foundation in management, operations, and strategy.
majors.description: Business administration is a general management degree: accounting, finance, marketing, operations, organizational behavior, and strategy, plus economics and statistics. It is broad by design and often paired with a concentration.
example_careers: Entertainment and Recreation Managers, Except Gambling

majors.name: Entrepreneurship
majors.blurb: Starting and growing new ventures.
majors.description: Entrepreneurship focuses on starting and growing new ventures: opportunity assessment, business models, financing, and the practical work of launching, often including running a real project. It draws on the rest of the business curriculum applied to early-stage companies.

majors.name: Finance
majors.blurb: Investment, valuation, capital markets, and corporate financial decisions.
majors.description: Finance studies how money is raised, invested, and managed: valuation, capital markets, corporate financial decisions, risk, and portfolio management. It builds on accounting, economics, and statistics and leads to corporate finance, investing, and banking roles.
example_careers: Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialists
Appraisers of Personal and Business Property

majors.name: Hospitality & Tourism Management
majors.blurb: Running hotels, restaurants, events, and travel businesses.
majors.description: Hospitality and tourism management is the business of hotels, restaurants, events, and travel: operations, service, revenue management, marketing, and finance for these industries, usually with substantial required work experience.
example_careers: Entertainment and Recreation Managers, Except Gambling

majors.name: Human Resources
majors.blurb: Hiring, developing, and supporting the people in an organization.
majors.description: Human resources management covers hiring, developing, compensating, and supporting the people in an organization, along with employment law, labor relations, and organizational behavior. It sits within business and is people- and policy-oriented.
example_careers: Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialists
Human Resources Assistants, Except Payroll and Timekeeping

majors.name: Management Information Systems
majors.blurb: The business side of technology: systems, data, and process.
majors.description: Management information systems is the business side of technology: databases, systems analysis and design, project management, business process, and data analytics. It bridges IT and management and does not require the depth of programming that computer science does.

majors.name: Marketing
majors.blurb: Understanding customers and bringing products to them.
majors.description: Marketing studies how to understand customers and bring products to them: consumer behavior, market research, branding, pricing, distribution, and increasingly digital and analytics. It blends quantitative analysis with strategy and creative work.
example_careers: Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists

majors.name: Real Estate
majors.blurb: Property markets, development, valuation, and investment.
majors.description: Real estate covers property markets, development, valuation, finance, and investment. It combines finance and economics with law and market analysis specific to land and buildings.
example_careers: Appraisers of Personal and Business Property
Appraisers and Assessors of Real Estate
Property, Real Estate, and Community Association Managers

majors.name: Sport Management
majors.blurb: The business of athletics: teams, venues, events, and media.
majors.description: Sport management is the business of athletics: teams, leagues, venues, events, sponsorship, and media. It applies management, marketing, finance, and law to the sport industry, usually with an internship.
example_careers: Entertainment and Recreation Managers, Except Gambling
Exercise Trainers and Group Fitness Instructors
Recreation and Fitness Studies Teachers, Postsecondary

majors.name: Supply Chain & Operations
majors.blurb: Getting products made and moved: logistics, sourcing, and operations.
majors.description: Supply chain and operations management is about getting products made and moved efficiently: sourcing, production planning, inventory, logistics, and process improvement. It is quantitative, using operations research and analytics, and highly employable.
example_careers: First-Line Supervisors of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
First-Line Supervisors of Production and Operating Workers

majors.name: Computer Science
majors.blurb: Algorithms, systems, and the theory behind how software works.
majors.description: Computer science is the study of computation itself: what problems can be solved, how efficiently, and how to build the software that solves them. Coursework runs from theory (algorithms, data structures, the limits of computation) to systems (operating systems, networks, databases) and usually a math core in discrete structures and probability. It is a broad foundation for software work, research, and most technical roles that involve building things.
example_careers: Software Quality Assurance Analysts and Testers

majors.name: Cybersecurity
majors.blurb: Defending systems and networks against attackers.
majors.description: Cybersecurity is the study of protecting systems, networks, and data from attack. Coursework covers cryptography, network and operating-system security, secure coding, digital forensics, risk, and often the policy and legal side. It sits between computer science and IT, with a strong hands-on component.
example_careers: Criminal Justice and Law Enforcement Teachers, Postsecondary

majors.name: Data Science
majors.blurb: Turning data into models and decisions with statistics and code.
majors.description: Data science combines statistics, programming, and domain knowledge to turn data into models and decisions. You study probability and statistical inference, machine learning, data wrangling and visualization, and often databases and a bit of software engineering. The work ranges from analysis and dashboards to building predictive models.

majors.name: Informatics
majors.blurb: How people, information, and technology fit together.
majors.description: Informatics studies how people, information, and technology fit together. It is more human-centered than computer science, drawing on design, social science, and information organization alongside programming, and often specializes in a domain like health, bioinformatics, or libraries.
example_careers: Software Quality Assurance Analysts and Testers

majors.name: Information Technology
majors.blurb: Running the networks, systems, and infrastructure organizations depend on.
majors.description: Information technology is about running the computing infrastructure organizations depend on: networks, servers, cloud services, security, and user support. It is more applied and operations-focused than computer science, with less theory and more hands-on configuration, administration, and troubleshooting.

majors.name: Software Engineering
majors.blurb: Building and maintaining large software systems as an engineering discipline.
majors.description: Software engineering focuses on building and maintaining large software systems as a discipline: requirements, design, testing, version control, deployment, and working on a team. It overlaps heavily with computer science but spends more time on the practices that keep a codebase healthy over years and less on theory. Graduates typically go directly into development roles.
example_careers: Software Quality Assurance Analysts and Testers

majors.name: Early Childhood Education
majors.blurb: Teaching and caring for children from birth through the early grades.
majors.description: Early childhood education focuses on teaching and caring for children from birth through the early grades, with heavy emphasis on child development, play-based learning, family engagement, and observation.
example_careers: Teaching Assistants, Preschool, Elementary, Middle, and Secondary School, Except Special Education
Elementary School Teachers, Except Special Education

majors.name: Elementary Education
majors.blurb: Teaching across subjects in the early grades.
majors.description: Elementary education prepares teachers for the early grades, covering child development, how to teach reading, math, science, and social studies to young children, classroom management, and assessment, with a supervised student-teaching placement and a path to state licensure.
example_careers: Elementary School Teachers, Except Special Education

majors.name: Secondary Education
majors.blurb: Teaching a subject at the middle- and high-school level.
majors.description: Secondary education prepares middle- and high-school teachers in a specific subject, pairing that subject's coursework with methods classes, adolescent development, and classroom practice, plus student teaching and licensure.
example_careers: Secondary School Teachers, Except Special and Career/Technical Education

majors.name: Special Education
majors.blurb: Teaching students with disabilities and designing individualized support.
majors.description: Special education prepares teachers to work with students with disabilities: assessment, individualized education programs, instructional strategies, behavior support, and the laws that govern services. It includes substantial supervised practice and licensure.

majors.name: Aerospace Engineering
majors.blurb: Aircraft, spacecraft, propulsion, and flight.
majors.description: Aerospace engineering is the design of aircraft, spacecraft, and their propulsion. It builds on mechanical engineering with added coursework in aerodynamics, flight mechanics, propulsion, structures, and control. Work spans commercial aviation, defense, and space.

majors.name: Aviation / Professional Flight
majors.blurb: Flying aircraft professionally, and the systems around it.
majors.description: Aviation or professional flight programs train pilots and cover the systems around flying: aerodynamics, aircraft systems, meteorology, air-traffic and airspace regulations, navigation, and crew resource management. Flight training toward FAA certificates and ratings is a central part of the degree.
example_careers: Airline Pilots, Copilots, and Flight Engineers

majors.name: Biomedical Engineering
majors.blurb: Applying engineering to medicine: devices, imaging, prosthetics, tissue.
majors.description: Biomedical engineering applies engineering to medicine and biology: medical devices, imaging, prosthetics, biomechanics, tissue engineering, and instrumentation. It is interdisciplinary, combining a chosen engineering track (mechanical, electrical, materials, or chemical) with anatomy, physiology, and biology.

majors.name: Chemical Engineering
majors.blurb: Designing processes that turn raw materials into products at scale.
majors.description: Chemical engineering applies chemistry, physics, and math to designing processes that convert raw materials into products at industrial scale. Core topics are material and energy balances, thermodynamics, reaction engineering, transport phenomena, and process control. Fields include energy, pharmaceuticals, materials, food, and the environment.

majors.name: Civil Engineering
majors.blurb: Roads, bridges, water systems, and the built environment.
majors.description: Civil engineering designs and maintains the built environment: buildings, bridges, roads, water and wastewater systems, and public infrastructure. Coursework covers structural analysis, geotechnical engineering, transportation, hydraulics, and construction, with an emphasis on safety codes and public responsibility.

majors.name: Computer Engineering
majors.blurb: Where hardware meets software: chips, embedded systems, and architecture.
majors.description: Computer engineering sits where hardware meets software. You study digital logic, computer architecture, embedded systems, and signal processing along with a solid chunk of electrical engineering, plus enough programming to work close to the metal. It leads to work on chips, devices, firmware, and systems.
example_careers: Software Quality Assurance Analysts and Testers

majors.name: Construction Management
majors.blurb: Planning, budgeting, and running building projects.
majors.description: Construction management is the business and coordination side of building projects: estimating, scheduling, budgeting, contracts, safety, and site supervision. It blends construction knowledge with project management, and graduates run projects rather than design the structures.

majors.name: Electrical Engineering
majors.blurb: Circuits, signals, power, and electronics.
majors.description: Electrical engineering is the study of electricity, electronics, and electromagnetic systems: circuits, signals and systems, electromagnetics, power, control, and communications, built on a heavy math and physics core. It is one of the broadest engineering fields, spanning power grids, chips, wireless, and instrumentation.

majors.name: Environmental Engineering
majors.blurb: Engineering for clean water, clean air, and waste.
majors.description: Environmental engineering applies engineering to clean water, clean air, and waste. Coursework covers water and wastewater treatment, air-quality control, solid and hazardous waste, environmental chemistry and microbiology, and the regulations that govern them. It is closely related to civil engineering.
example_careers: Health and Safety Engineers, Except Mining Safety Engineers and Inspectors

majors.name: General Engineering
majors.blurb: A broad engineering foundation before specializing.
majors.description: General or undeclared engineering gives a broad first-year-and-beyond foundation, math, physics, computing, and introductory design, before you commit to a specialty. Some programs keep it general throughout for students headed toward interdisciplinary or management roles.

majors.name: Industrial Engineering
majors.blurb: Making systems of people, machines, and materials run efficiently.
majors.description: Industrial engineering optimizes systems of people, machines, materials, and information. Coursework covers operations research, statistics and quality, supply-chain and logistics, human factors, and simulation. Graduates work on efficiency, planning, and process improvement across manufacturing, healthcare, and services.

majors.name: Materials Science & Engineering
majors.blurb: Why materials behave the way they do, and designing better ones.
majors.description: Materials science and engineering studies why materials behave as they do and how to design better ones. It connects structure at the atomic and microscopic scale to properties and processing, covering metals, ceramics, polymers, semiconductors, and composites.

majors.name: Mechanical Engineering
majors.blurb: Machines, mechanisms, energy, and how physical things are made to move.
majors.description: Mechanical engineering deals with forces, motion, energy, and how physical things are designed and made. Core coursework covers statics and dynamics, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, materials, heat transfer, and machine design. It is the most general engineering major and touches nearly every industry that builds physical products.

majors.name: Robotics Engineering
majors.blurb: Mechatronics, control, and autonomous machines.
majors.description: Robotics engineering is an interdisciplinary field combining mechanical design, electronics, control theory, and software to build machines that sense and act in the world. Coursework covers kinematics and dynamics, sensors and actuators, control, computer vision, and autonomy.

majors.name: Agricultural Science
majors.blurb: The science and business of growing food and fiber.
majors.description: Agricultural science is the science and business of growing food and fiber, spanning soils, crops, plant and animal production, agricultural economics, and increasingly agricultural technology and data. Programs are applied and often tied to a specific commodity or system.
example_careers: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
Farmers, Ranchers, and Other Agricultural Managers

majors.name: Animal Science
majors.blurb: The biology, care, and production of domestic animals.
majors.description: Animal science studies the biology, nutrition, genetics, reproduction, health, and management of domestic animals, mostly livestock and companion animals. It is a common pre-veterinary path and also leads into production agriculture and animal industries.
example_careers: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
Farmers, Ranchers, and Other Agricultural Managers

majors.name: Environmental Science
majors.blurb: The science of ecosystems, pollution, and environmental change.
majors.description: Environmental science is the natural-science study of ecosystems, pollution, and environmental change, integrating biology, chemistry, geology, and often data analysis. It is field- and lab-oriented and leads to work in monitoring, remediation, conservation, and consulting.
example_careers: Environmental Scientists and Specialists, Including Health
Environmental Science and Protection Technicians, Including Health

majors.name: Environmental Studies
majors.blurb: Environmental problems through policy, economics, and the social sciences.
majors.description: Environmental studies approaches environmental problems through policy, economics, ethics, and the social sciences, alongside a grounding in environmental science. It is interdisciplinary and aimed at policy, advocacy, planning, and management.
example_careers: Environmental Scientists and Specialists, Including Health

majors.name: Food Science
majors.blurb: The chemistry, safety, and engineering of the food supply.
majors.description: Food science applies chemistry, microbiology, and engineering to the food supply: food chemistry, processing, safety, quality, and product development. It is lab- and industry-oriented and highly employable in food manufacturing and regulation.

majors.name: Forestry & Natural Resources
majors.blurb: Managing forests, rangelands, and wild lands.
majors.description: Forestry and natural resource management prepare people to manage forests, rangelands, and wild lands for timber, water, wildlife, recreation, and ecosystem health, combining ecology and silviculture with measurement, GIS, and policy, and a strong field component.
example_careers: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
Forestry and Conservation Science Teachers, Postsecondary

majors.name: Sustainability
majors.blurb: Balancing human needs with the limits of natural systems.
majors.description: Sustainability studies focus on balancing human needs with the limits of natural systems, spanning energy, climate, resources, business, and policy. It is interdisciplinary and systems-oriented, connecting environmental science with economics and management.
example_careers: Environmental Scientists and Specialists, Including Health
Environmental Science and Protection Technicians, Including Health
Forestry and Conservation Science Teachers, Postsecondary

majors.name: Wildlife & Fisheries
majors.blurb: Managing and conserving wild animal populations and their habitats.
majors.description: Wildlife and fisheries science study the biology, populations, and habitats of wild animals and how to conserve and manage them. It combines ecology, zoology, and quantitative methods with field techniques and wildlife and fisheries policy.
example_careers: Forestry and Conservation Science Teachers, Postsecondary

majors.name: Athletic Training
majors.blurb: Preventing, assessing, and rehabilitating athletic injuries.
majors.description: Athletic training prepares clinicians who prevent, evaluate, and rehabilitate injuries, mostly in sport and physically active populations. It combines anatomy, physiology, and biomechanics with hands-on assessment and treatment skills and extensive clinical hours, and leads to certification.

majors.name: Communication Sciences & Disorders
majors.blurb: Speech, language, and hearing, and the disorders that affect them.
majors.description: Communication sciences and disorders is the study of speech, language, and hearing and the disorders that affect them. The undergraduate degree is a foundation, covering phonetics, anatomy of speech and hearing, language development, and audiology, before a graduate degree in speech-language pathology or audiology.

majors.name: Health Administration
majors.blurb: Running hospitals, clinics, and health systems.
majors.description: Health administration is the management side of healthcare: running hospitals, clinics, and health systems. Coursework covers health policy, economics, finance, operations, informatics, and law as they apply to care delivery.

majors.name: Kinesiology & Exercise Science
majors.blurb: How the body moves, and how training and rehab change it.
majors.description: Kinesiology and exercise science study how the human body moves and responds to physical activity: anatomy, exercise physiology, biomechanics, and motor control. It is a common path toward physical therapy, athletic training, strength and conditioning, and clinical or research work.

majors.name: Medical Laboratory Science
majors.blurb: The lab testing that diagnoses disease.
majors.description: Medical laboratory science trains the professionals who run the lab tests that diagnose and monitor disease: hematology, clinical chemistry, microbiology, immunology, and blood banking. The degree is heavy on lab technique and quality control and leads to certification.

majors.name: Nursing
majors.blurb: Direct patient care, assessment, and coordination across a care team.
majors.description: Nursing prepares registered nurses to provide direct patient care, assess and monitor conditions, administer treatments, educate patients, and coordinate across a care team. The degree combines anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, and pathophysiology with supervised clinical rotations, and leads to licensure by exam.

majors.name: Nutrition & Dietetics
majors.blurb: Food, metabolism, and how diet affects health.
majors.description: Nutrition and dietetics study food, metabolism, and how diet affects health across the lifespan and in disease. Coursework combines biochemistry and physiology with food science, community nutrition, and medical nutrition therapy. The registered-dietitian path adds a supervised internship and exam.

majors.name: Pre-Medicine
majors.blurb: A science track aimed at medical, dental, or veterinary school.
majors.description: Pre-medicine is not usually a major itself but a track: a science-heavy course load (biology, general and organic chemistry, biochemistry, physics, math, and often psychology and sociology) taken alongside any major to prepare for medical, dental, or veterinary school and the admissions exams.

majors.name: Public Health
majors.blurb: Preventing disease and improving health at the population level.
majors.description: Public health focuses on preventing disease and improving health at the population level rather than one patient at a time. Coursework covers epidemiology, biostatistics, health policy and management, environmental health, and health behavior. Roles range from data and program work to policy and community health.

majors.name: Africana / Black Studies
majors.blurb: The history, culture, and politics of African and African-descended peoples.
majors.description: Africana or Black studies examine the history, culture, politics, and social experience of African and African-descended peoples, across the continent and the diaspora. It is interdisciplinary, combining history, literature, sociology, and political science.
example_careers: Area, Ethnic, and Cultural Studies Teachers, Postsecondary

majors.name: American Studies
majors.blurb: US culture, history, and society across disciplines.
majors.description: American studies examines the culture, history, politics, and society of the United States across disciplines, often with a focus on race, class, gender, and power. It combines history, literature, and social science around American themes.
example_careers: Area, Ethnic, and Cultural Studies Teachers, Postsecondary

majors.name: Classics
majors.blurb: The languages, literature, and history of ancient Greece and Rome.
majors.description: Classics is the study of the languages, literature, history, and culture of ancient Greece and Rome. Learning Latin and ancient Greek is usually central, alongside coursework in ancient history, philosophy, and archaeology.
example_careers: Foreign Language and Literature Teachers, Postsecondary
Secondary School Teachers, Except Special and Career/Technical Education

majors.name: Creative Writing
majors.blurb: The craft of fiction, poetry, and nonfiction.
majors.description: Creative writing focuses on the craft of fiction, poetry, and creative nonfiction, taught largely through workshops where students write and critique. It usually sits within an English department and pairs practice with reading widely.
example_careers: English Language and Literature Teachers, Postsecondary

majors.name: English
majors.blurb: Literature, criticism, and writing.
majors.description: English is the study of literature, language, and writing. Coursework spans literary history and criticism, close reading and analysis, and a lot of writing. It builds strong reading, argument, and communication skills and leads to many fields, not just teaching.
example_careers: English Language and Literature Teachers, Postsecondary
Secondary School Teachers, Except Special and Career/Technical Education

majors.name: Gender & Women's Studies
majors.blurb: Gender and sexuality as they shape culture, politics, and everyday life.
majors.description: Gender and women's studies examine how gender and sexuality shape culture, politics, institutions, and everyday life. It is interdisciplinary, drawing on history, sociology, literature, and philosophy, with an emphasis on power and social change.
example_careers: Area, Ethnic, and Cultural Studies Teachers, Postsecondary

majors.name: History
majors.blurb: The human past, and how we reconstruct and argue about it.
majors.description: History is the study of the human past and the methods for reconstructing and arguing about it from evidence. Students choose regional and thematic concentrations and write research papers using primary sources. It develops research, synthesis, and written argument.
example_careers: Secondary School Teachers, Except Special and Career/Technical Education

majors.name: Liberal Arts / Interdisciplinary Studies
majors.blurb: A broad, self-directed path across the arts and sciences.
majors.description: Liberal arts or interdisciplinary studies is a broad, often self-directed path across the arts, humanities, and sciences, sometimes built around a custom theme. It emphasizes breadth, writing, and critical thinking over a single specialization.
example_careers: Area, Ethnic, and Cultural Studies Teachers, Postsecondary

majors.name: Linguistics
majors.blurb: The structure of language: sound, meaning, grammar, and change.
majors.description: Linguistics is the scientific study of language: its sound systems (phonetics and phonology), structure (morphology and syntax), meaning (semantics), and how it varies and changes. It is analytical and increasingly computational, and connects to psychology, computer science, and anthropology.
example_careers: Foreign Language and Literature Teachers, Postsecondary

majors.name: Philosophy
majors.blurb: Argument about knowledge, ethics, mind, and reality.
majors.description: Philosophy is the study of fundamental questions about knowledge, reality, mind, ethics, and logic through careful argument. Areas include logic, ethics, metaphysics, epistemology, and the history of philosophy. It is training in precise reasoning and analysis.

majors.name: Religious Studies
majors.blurb: Religious traditions, texts, and practices, studied academically.
majors.description: Religious studies examines religious traditions, texts, practices, and their role in societies, studied academically rather than devotionally. It draws on history, philosophy, anthropology, and textual analysis, often with a language component.

majors.name: World Languages & Cultures
majors.blurb: A modern language (Spanish, French, Mandarin, ...) plus the literature and culture behind it.
majors.description: A world languages major develops advanced proficiency in a modern language such as Spanish, French, Mandarin, or Japanese, along with the literature, history, and culture of the places where it is spoken. Coursework is conducted largely in the target language, and study abroad is common.
example_careers: English Language and Literature Teachers, Postsecondary
Foreign Language and Literature Teachers, Postsecondary
Secondary School Teachers, Except Special and Career/Technical Education

majors.name: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology
majors.blurb: The chemistry of life: proteins, DNA, metabolism, and cell machinery.
majors.description: Biochemistry and molecular biology study the chemistry of life: proteins, nucleic acids, metabolism, and the molecular machinery of cells. It combines an organic and physical chemistry core with cell and molecular biology and heavy laboratory work.

majors.name: Biology
majors.blurb: Living systems from molecules to ecosystems.
majors.description: Biology is the study of living systems across scales, from molecules and cells to organisms and ecosystems. Core coursework includes cell and molecular biology, genetics, evolution, physiology, and ecology, plus chemistry and often physics and statistics. It is a broad major that feeds medicine, research, education, and industry.

majors.name: Ecology & Evolutionary Biology
majors.blurb: How organisms interact with each other and their environment over time.
majors.description: Ecology and evolutionary biology study how organisms interact with each other and their environment, and how populations change over time. Coursework covers population and community ecology, evolution, biodiversity, and quantitative methods, with field and lab components.

majors.name: Genetics
majors.blurb: Heredity, genomes, and how genes shape organisms.
majors.description: Genetics studies heredity and the genome: how genes are structured, expressed, inherited, and edited, and how genetic variation shapes organisms and disease. It builds on molecular and cell biology with added coursework in genomics and bioinformatics.

majors.name: Marine Biology
majors.blurb: Life in the oceans, from plankton to whales.
majors.description: Marine biology studies life in the oceans, from plankton and invertebrates to fish and marine mammals, and the ecosystems they form. It is a specialization within biology with added coursework in oceanography and marine ecology, and a strong field emphasis.

majors.name: Microbiology
majors.blurb: Bacteria, viruses, and other microbes, and their role in health and disease.
majors.description: Microbiology studies bacteria, viruses, fungi, and other microbes: their biology, genetics, and roles in health, disease, agriculture, and the environment. It combines cell and molecular biology with substantial lab technique in culturing and identification.

majors.name: Neuroscience
majors.blurb: How the brain and nervous system produce behavior and cognition.
majors.description: Neuroscience studies the brain and nervous system and how they produce behavior and cognition. It is interdisciplinary, spanning molecular and cellular neuroscience, systems and circuits, and cognitive and behavioral approaches, with coursework in biology, chemistry, psychology, and statistics.

majors.name: Zoology
majors.blurb: Animal biology, behavior, and physiology.
majors.description: Zoology is the study of animals: their anatomy, physiology, behavior, evolution, and ecology, from invertebrates to vertebrates. It overlaps with biology and often leads toward wildlife, veterinary, or research paths.

majors.name: Communication
majors.blurb: How messages move through people, organizations, and media.
majors.description: Communication studies how messages move through people, organizations, and media, covering interpersonal and group communication, rhetoric, media theory, and often public speaking and writing. It is broad and applied, feeding roles in PR, marketing, media, and human resources.
example_careers: Broadcast Announcers and Radio Disc Jockeys

majors.name: Digital & Multimedia
majors.blurb: Web, social, video, and interactive content.
majors.description: Digital and multimedia programs cover creating content for web, social, video, and interactive platforms: design, video and audio production, web basics, and storytelling. They sit between communication and design and are strongly project-based.

majors.name: Journalism
majors.blurb: Reporting, writing, and producing the news.
majors.description: Journalism trains reporters and producers to gather, verify, write, and present the news across print, broadcast, and digital. Coursework covers reporting and writing, media law and ethics, and multimedia production, with real reporting throughout.

majors.name: Public Relations & Advertising
majors.blurb: Shaping how organizations are seen, and moving audiences to act.
majors.description: Public relations and advertising focus on shaping how organizations are seen and moving audiences to act: strategy, messaging, media relations, campaigns, and increasingly social and digital media. Coursework combines communication theory with writing and campaign work.

majors.name: Astronomy & Astrophysics
majors.blurb: Stars, galaxies, cosmology, and the physics of the universe.
majors.description: Astronomy and astrophysics study stars, planets, galaxies, and the universe as a whole, applying physics to objects we mostly cannot experiment on. It shares a physics core and adds coursework in stellar and galactic astrophysics, cosmology, and observational techniques.
example_careers: Atmospheric, Earth, Marine, and Space Sciences Teachers, Postsecondary

majors.name: Atmospheric Science & Meteorology
majors.blurb: Weather, climate, and the physics of the atmosphere.
majors.description: Atmospheric science and meteorology study the physics and chemistry of the atmosphere: weather systems, forecasting, atmospheric dynamics, radiation, and climate. It is math- and physics-heavy and increasingly involves large datasets and modeling.
example_careers: Atmospheric, Earth, Marine, and Space Sciences Teachers, Postsecondary

majors.name: Chemistry
majors.blurb: Matter at the level of atoms and molecules, and the reactions between them.
majors.description: Chemistry studies matter at the level of atoms and molecules and the reactions between them. The core covers general, organic, inorganic, analytical, and physical chemistry, with substantial laboratory work. It underpins medicine, materials, energy, and biology.
example_careers: Secondary School Teachers, Except Special and Career/Technical Education

majors.name: Geology & Earth Science
majors.blurb: The Earth's materials, structure, and history.
majors.description: Geology, or earth science, studies the Earth's materials, structure, and history, from minerals and rocks to plate tectonics, surface processes, and deep time. Coursework combines field work with chemistry, physics, and often data analysis, and connects to energy, water, hazards, and the environment.
example_careers: Atmospheric, Earth, Marine, and Space Sciences Teachers, Postsecondary

majors.name: Mathematics
majors.blurb: Proof, structure, and abstraction, pure and applied.
majors.description: Mathematics is the study of structure, quantity, and change through proof. A typical path runs from calculus and linear algebra into real analysis, abstract algebra, and topology, with electives in areas like number theory, geometry, or applied math. It develops rigorous reasoning that transfers widely.
example_careers: Secondary School Teachers, Except Special and Career/Technical Education

majors.name: Oceanography
majors.blurb: The physics, chemistry, and biology of the oceans.
majors.description: Oceanography studies the physics, chemistry, biology, and geology of the oceans as a connected system, from currents and waves to marine ecosystems and seafloor geology. It is interdisciplinary and field-oriented, with a strong quantitative core.

majors.name: Physics
majors.blurb: The fundamental laws governing matter, energy, space, and time.
majors.description: Physics is the study of the fundamental laws governing matter, energy, space, and time. The core sequence covers classical mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum mechanics, thermodynamics and statistical mechanics, all built on heavy mathematics, with lab work throughout.
example_careers: Secondary School Teachers, Except Special and Career/Technical Education

majors.name: Statistics
majors.blurb: Reasoning about uncertainty and drawing conclusions from data.
majors.description: Statistics is the science of learning from data under uncertainty: how to design studies, estimate quantities, test hypotheses, and quantify how much to trust a conclusion. Coursework covers probability, statistical inference, regression, experimental design, and computing, and increasingly overlaps with data science and machine learning.

majors.name: Cognitive Science
majors.blurb: Mind and intelligence across psychology, neuroscience, linguistics, and AI.
majors.description: Cognitive science studies the mind and intelligence across disciplines: psychology, neuroscience, linguistics, philosophy, and artificial intelligence. It asks how thinking works in both brains and machines, and blends experiment, theory, and computation.

majors.name: Human Development & Family Studies
majors.blurb: How people grow and change across the lifespan, in families and communities.
majors.description: Human development and family studies examine how people grow and change across the lifespan, within families and communities. Coursework covers developmental psychology, family systems, and applied topics like early intervention, aging, and family policy.
example_careers: Educational, Guidance, and Career Counselors and Advisors
Child, Family, and School Social Workers
Family and Consumer Sciences Teachers, Postsecondary

majors.name: Psychology
majors.blurb: The science of mind and behavior.
majors.description: Psychology is the scientific study of mind and behavior, covering cognition, development, social behavior, personality, and mental health, along with the biological basis of behavior. Research methods and statistics are central. The bachelor's is broad; clinical practice requires graduate training.

majors.name: Parks, Recreation & Leisure
majors.blurb: Programming and managing parks, recreation, and the outdoors.
majors.description: Parks, recreation, and leisure studies prepare people to program and manage parks, recreation departments, outdoor and adventure programs, and community services, covering programming, facility and event management, and often environmental interpretation.
example_careers: Recreation and Fitness Studies Teachers, Postsecondary

majors.name: Public Administration
majors.blurb: Managing government agencies and public programs.
majors.description: Public administration is the management of government agencies and public programs: budgeting, policy implementation, human resources, and ethics in the public sector. It is the public-sector counterpart to a management degree.

majors.name: Public Policy
majors.blurb: Analyzing and designing the policies governments adopt.
majors.description: Public policy analyzes and designs the policies governments adopt, using economics, statistics, and political science to weigh costs, benefits, and tradeoffs. It is analytical and problem-focused, often ending in a capstone client project.

majors.name: Social Work
majors.blurb: Helping individuals and families navigate hardship and systems.
majors.description: Social work helps individuals and families cope with hardship and navigate systems, and works to change those systems. Coursework covers human behavior, social policy, and practice skills, with supervised field placements. Clinical practice generally requires a master's and licensure.
example_careers: Child, Family, and School Social Workers
Mental Health and Substance Abuse Social Workers
Probation Officers and Correctional Treatment Specialists

majors.name: Anthropology
majors.blurb: Human cultures, past and present, and what makes us human.
majors.description: Anthropology is the study of humans across time and cultures. It has four traditional branches: cultural, biological, linguistic, and archaeological. Fieldwork and the comparative method are central, and it develops a close-observation, cross-cultural perspective.

majors.name: Criminology & Criminal Justice
majors.blurb: Crime, the justice system, and how society responds to both.
majors.description: Criminology and criminal justice study crime, the justice system, and how society responds to both: the causes of crime, policing, courts, corrections, and policy. It draws on sociology, psychology, and law, with training in research methods.
example_careers: Criminal Justice and Law Enforcement Teachers, Postsecondary

majors.name: Economics
majors.blurb: How people, firms, and governments allocate scarce resources.
majors.description: Economics studies how people, firms, and governments allocate scarce resources and respond to incentives. The core is microeconomics, macroeconomics, and econometrics, built on calculus and statistics. It is analytical rather than business-focused and feeds finance, policy, data, and academia.
example_careers: Secondary School Teachers, Except Special and Career/Technical Education

majors.name: Geography
majors.blurb: Places, spatial patterns, and the relationship between people and land.
majors.description: Geography studies places, spatial patterns, and the relationship between people and the environment. It spans physical geography (landforms, climate) and human geography (cities, migration, economies), and increasingly centers on geographic information systems (GIS) and spatial data.

majors.name: International Relations
majors.blurb: Diplomacy, conflict, trade, and how countries deal with each other.
majors.description: International relations studies how states and other actors interact: diplomacy, conflict and security, trade, international law, and global institutions. It combines political science with economics, history, and usually a foreign language and regional focus.

majors.name: Political Science
majors.blurb: Government, power, institutions, and political behavior.
majors.description: Political science studies government, power, institutions, and political behavior. Subfields include American politics, comparative politics, international relations, and political theory, with growing use of quantitative methods.
example_careers: Secondary School Teachers, Except Special and Career/Technical Education

majors.name: Sociology
majors.blurb: How groups, institutions, and social structures shape behavior.
majors.description: Sociology studies how groups, institutions, and social structures shape behavior, covering inequality, family, crime, work, race, and social change. It teaches both qualitative and quantitative research methods and a habit of looking for patterns beyond the individual.

majors.name: Urban Studies & Planning
majors.blurb: How cities work, and how to make them work better.
majors.description: Urban studies and planning examine how cities work and how to shape them: land use, transportation, housing, the economy, and the environment. It is interdisciplinary and applied, with studio and policy work alongside social-science coursework.
